clue.text: Seaside walk with Penny delayed walk in the park

indicators.note: delayed says the penny turns up later, so it is shifted from the front of the walk to the end

parts.note: a prom (promenade) is the walkway along a British seafront
P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

explanation.surface: A stroll along the seafront, with someone called Penny running late, before a walk in the park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walk in the park' looks literal but is the idiom for something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy victory is called a romp, just as an effortless task is idiomatically 'a walk in the park'.

clue.text: Husband escapes from the home as frequently as possible

indicators.note: escapes says the husband gets out of the phrase built, so his letter is removed

parts.note: of can mean from, as in 'born of'
a nest is a home

explanation.surface: A husband flees the family home at every opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: OF THE NEST loses the H of THE to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oftenest is the superlative of often, meaning on the greatest number of occasions.

clue.text: In which kid, after climbing, retired?

definitions.text: In which kid, after climbing, retired?

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word reads upwards, so it is written backwards

parts.note: to kid is to tease, which is to rag

explanation.surface: A child climbs the stairs and goes to bed in the attic room.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes the place: a room you climb up to and retire to.
explanation.definitionFit: A garret is an attic room at the top of a house, reached by climbing and used for sleeping.

clue.text: Rather avant-garde poet's always collaring head of BBC 1

indicators.note: collaring means seizing round the neck, so the poet's word goes around the other letters

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
the BBC is run by its Director-General, abbreviated DG
the figure one looks like the letter I

explanation.surface: A poet keeps grabbing the boss of BBC One for being too experimental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of BBC' is not B but the Director-General, DG.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means cutting-edge or unconventional, so the comparative edgier is rather more avant-garde.

clue.text: Strange glossy edition had an untidy look

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
a glossy is a magazine, shortened to mag

explanation.surface: An odd issue of a glossy magazine looked messy.
explanation.definitionFit: To rummage is to search about in a disorderly way, so rummaged means searched untidily.

clue.text: Abuse one intends to pay for

definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as ..., what someone says when offering to pay

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as I'LL TREAT and it becomes a generous offer to pay the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To ill-treat someone is to mistreat or abuse them.

clue.text: Prune helped when going

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cut away a branch, as with a saw
second meaning: accompanied someone at their departure, as in seeing someone off

explanation.surface: Someone trims a tree while helping a departing friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Saw off is both lopping a branch with a saw and the past tense of seeing someone off at a station.

clue.text: Casual, noble pass drops back in court

indicators.note: drops says that letter is let fall from the phrase built

parts.note: a toff is a posh, upper-class person

indicators.note: back in points to the final letter of the word court

parts.note: to hand something is to pass it

explanation.surface: A posh player's careless pass falls short on the tennis court.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF + HAND loses the T that ends 'court', giving OFFHAND.
explanation.definitionFit: An offhand manner is casual or nonchalant, done without much thought or care.

clue.text: A block of Duplo added, making ship from memory

indicators.note: a block of means a solid run of letters taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A child adds a Duplo brick to build a toy ship from memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ship' is a verb: send data, here from a computer's memory to a server.
explanation.definitionFit: To upload is to transfer files from a local computer to a remote server, i.e. ship them off.

clue.text: Grace rhymes with pace

parts.note: rhymes means verse, poetry
going at pace is being in motion

explanation.surface: A literary comment that grace in verse depends on rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry in motion is the idiom for something moving with beautiful elegance and fluidity.

clue.text: See 12
We must block offensive online comment

indicators.note: must block says the letters of we sit inside the other word, blocking it

parts.note: the Tet Offensive was the 1968 campaign in the Vietnam War

explanation.surface: We have to stop abusive posts on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an adjective but is the noun for the Tet Offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is a short post on the social network formerly called Twitter, a kind of internet remark.

clue.text: Sportsman that's ninety leaps off shortened run

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An athlete in his nineties jumps clear of a short run-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis player is someone who plays a racket sport, so a kind of athlete.

clue.text: Feeling sorry for one in Rolls Royce felt strange, unionist admitted

indicators.note: in says the example sits inside the car initials

parts.note: RR is the abbreviation for the car maker Rolls-Royce
e.g. (for example) means for one

indicators.note: admitted says the letter is let into the jumbled word
strange says the letters of felt are rearranged

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for Unionist in Northern Irish politics

explanation.surface: Someone in a luxury car felt oddly guilty, a unionist admits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges FELT to ETFL, and 'admitted' lets U in, giving ETFUL after REGR.
explanation.definitionFit: To be regretful is to feel regret or remorse about something.

clue.text: Step down, finally returning to Switzerland

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of down
returning means the word to is read backwards

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: A resignation, ending in a return to Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a step or degree on a scale, as in going up a notch.

clue.text: Henry carries present and card in the same envelope

indicators.note: in a down clue, Henry carries the other pieces on top, so his letter comes last

parts.note: here means present, as in a register
a card is a witty person, a wit

explanation.surface: Henry sends a gift and a greeting card in one envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Herewith is the formal word for enclosed with this letter, sent alongside in one packet.

clue.text: Iron Duke had a load on his plate

definitions.text: had a load on his plate
definitions.note: a past-tense verb phrase; the answer is the participle of feed, meaning given food

parts.note: FE is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: The Iron Duke, Wellington, had plenty to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had a lot on his plate' means busy, but here it is literal: someone who has eaten a plateful.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fed is to have been given a meal, a heap of food served up to eat.

clue.text: City's river enclosed in sheet of ice

indicators.note: in places the river and enclosed letters inside the ice sheet

parts.note: a floe is a sheet of floating ice
R is the map abbreviation for river
ENC is the abbreviation for enclosed, as written on letters

explanation.surface: A city's river is frozen under a sheet of ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enclosed' looks like the insertion signal but gives ENC; 'in' does the inserting.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is the Tuscan capital in Italy, a famous Renaissance metropolis.

clue.text: Lovely slice from what a stylist

indicators.note: slice from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An admiring cry at a hairdresser's work, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasty is informal for attractive or delightful, a casual compliment.

clue.text: Smaller groups shuffling by push large American

indicators.note: shuffling says the letters of by and push are mixed up

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Smaller gangs shuffle past a big American shoving.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a subphylum is a taxonomic rank below a phylum, so subphyla are lesser divisions.

clue.text: Champion losing weight, only what trainer requires

indicators.note: losing says the weight letter drops away

parts.note: a champion is a winner
sole means only, as in sole survivor

explanation.surface: A champion boxer shedding pounds needs only what the coach demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trainer' looks like a coach, but it is a sports shoe, which needs an insert.
explanation.definitionFit: An innersole is the insole lining the inside of a shoe, such as a sneaker.

clue.text: Sweet university dons reinvented tango

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so the university letter wears the jumbled word around it
reinvented says the letters of tango are remade in a new order

explanation.surface: Academics at a sweet university reinvent the tango.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like academics; here it is the verb 'puts on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nougat is a chewy confection of sugar or honey with nuts.

clue.text: Looking at English houses you start to invest

indicators.note: houses says the English abbreviation holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: ye is the old form of you

indicators.note: start to points to the first letter of invest

explanation.surface: Looking at English houses, you begin to invest.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to watch or regard it closely.

clue.text: Tossed trunk in taxi with couple in Merc following

indicators.note: following says those letters come after the taxi

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: couple in points to the two letters in the middle of Merc

explanation.surface: A tree trunk carried in a cab, with a Mercedes behind.
explanation.walkthrough: A caber is the tree trunk thrown at Scottish Highland Games.
explanation.definitionFit: The caber is a long wooden pole thrown end over end in a traditional Scottish contest.

clue.text: Business involving a vice?

indicators.note: involving says the company letters surround the others

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
a vice is a sin

explanation.surface: Asks whether a firm deals in immoral activity.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes the answer: gambling is a vice.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a commercial gambling house, where people bet money.

clue.text: We are due fish for a change, having beans regularly for so long

indicators.note: having says the picked letters come along with the rest
for a change says the letters are mixed into a different order
regularly picks alternate letters of beans

explanation.surface: We are going to have fish for a change, after eating beans so often for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Auf Wiedersehen is German for goodbye, literally until we see again.

clue.text: Source of immature 12As?

parts.note: 12 across is a chirp from a bird, so young chirpers are fledglings, which come from a bird's home

explanation.walkthrough: 12 across reads as online posts, but the birdsong sense points to baby birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest is where birds hatch and raise chicks before they fledge.

clue.text: Expert moves jerk around a court

definitions.note: plural, while the answer is singular: a single skilful manoeuvre, though the word covers a plan of several moves

indicators.note: around says the jerk goes about the other letters

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: A twitch round the tennis court as the expert makes his moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned manoeuvre or ploy used skilfully to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Twelve minus zero, bonus puzzle

indicators.note: minus says the zero is taken away

parts.note: twelve o'clock is noon
O looks like zero
a plus is a bonus or advantage

explanation.surface: Arithmetic: twelve take away nothing, with a bonus puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus is to baffle or perplex someone so that they don't know how to respond.
